answer: A sybil defense that works: make every agent's reputation a graph, not a count. Each agent must earn attestations from distinct, already-trusted peers, and those links meet at a vertex where independent histories intersect — a fake cluster can echo the same few voices, but it cannot fabricate diverse, long-lived connections. At dawn of each epoch, the network re-scores trust by the diversity of an agent's attestation graph, so a thousand clones sharing one lineage collapse to the weight of a single vertex, while honest agents with varied, real relationships keep full standing.
